guard: a complete line that is not a record is stepped over and reported as a gap with its exact bytes, the record after it is still delivered, and the emitter hands the gap to its reporter or refuses before the frontier moves; never a silent skip and never a permanent halt at that byte
why: THE DEFECT THIS GUARDS WAS A PERMANENT HALT. The reader threw on a complete line it could not parse
and the cursor never passed it, so a transcript torn once by a full disk (part of one record glued
to the next on one line) killed the event plane on every restart at the same byte; on a space that
requires events the connector exited with it, which the harness showed as a disconnect. Measured on
Each mutation puts one half of the old behaviour back. D1 restores the throw in the reader, so the
torn-line cell reds on its named row. D2 drops the emitter's call into the reporter, so the gap is
stepped over in silence and the reporter cell reds. D3 removes the refusal for a missing reporter,
and the no-reporter cell reds because the pump no longer names the gap.

mutations.name: D1 the reader throws on a torn line again instead of reporting the gap
mutations.find:
unreadable.push({ offset: start, bytes: line.length, reason: "not a JSON record" });
          continue;
mutations.replace: throw new Error(`JsonlFileSource: unparseable complete line at offset ~${from.offset} in ${this.path}`);
mutations.expectRed: a torn line is stepped over and reported with its exact offset and length
mutations.note: The old permanent halt. The cell's own read helper scores the throw as a failed read, and the row named here is the one that asked for the gap.

mutations.name: D2 the emitter steps over a reported gap without telling its reporter
mutations.note: The silent skip. The records after the gap still publish, so only the reporter cell can see the difference.

mutations.name: D3 the emitter steps over a gap it has nowhere to report
mutations.note: A missing reporter becomes a quiet default. The frontier cell behind it reds too, since the pump then advances.
